obstacles: Growth by imbibition is not directly annotated.
Cell walls and cytoskeleton can generate planes without external pressure.
The scope extends from cells to whole organisms.
assessments.rationale: Surface geometry is readily measurable, and image repositories can test the predicted association in selected systems. Data do not consistently include material state and pressure, limiting causal discrimination and broad scope.

assessments.operationalization: Fit force-balance models to cell shapes using measured cortical or interfacial tension, gravity, pressure, osmosis, adhesion, and wall mechanics, then compare each factor's predictive contribution across representative cell types. Surface tension is paramount only if removing it causes the largest general loss of predictive accuracy.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Cell-mechanics perturbation imaging can test tension-dependent shape predictions.

obstacles: 'Paramount' needs an imposed quantitative criterion.
Most datasets do not measure all competing forces.
Walled and wall-less cells require different models.
assessments.rationale: Relative force contributions can be estimated in defined systems, but the global ranking is vague and all-cell scope is too broad. Existing data resolve selected cell types and perturbations, not the general claim.

assessments.operationalization: Quantify symmetry and dynamic equilibrium or shape fluctuations across resting and motile organisms, and test whether departures from equilibrium predict asymmetry after controlling lineage and function. A stable asymmetric organism or symmetric nonequilibrium state would refute the categorical relation.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Time-lapse imaging can relate symmetry to motility and shape fluctuations.

obstacles: Equilibrium and minimal energy are not directly observed from shape alone.
Biological symmetry is inherited and actively maintained.
The claim's exceptions and scope are vague.
assessments.rationale: Symmetry and dynamics can be measured, and obvious counterexamples could refute a strict reading. Demonstrating the proposed minimal-energy cause rather than developmental regulation requires matched force and energy measurements rarely available broadly.

assessments.operationalization: Track pseudopod-tip relaxation after local perturbation and compare curvature dynamics with capillary relaxation predictions; independently inhibit actomyosin contractility and alter membrane or cortical tension. Persistence of predicted rounding without active contraction supports the claim, while ATP-dependent contractile rounding refutes it.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Open amoeboid motility and cytoskeletal-perturbation movies permit curvature-dynamics analysis.

candidate_datasets.name: Cell Image Library
candidate_datasets.role: Public cell and amoeba images provide examples of pseudopod rounding and morphology.

obstacles: Modern cortical tension often arises from active contractility.
Direct tension measurements are uncommon.
Passive and active mechanisms may act together.
assessments.rationale: The passive-versus-active alternatives imply distinct energy dependence and perturbation responses. Existing movies can test selected systems, though direct force measurements and mechanistic separation are incomplete.

assessments.operationalization: Measure spatial surface-tension gradients and plasmodial flow during controlled moisture, temperature, nutrient, sugar, and salt gradients, then perturb tension independently of sensory signaling. Support requires direction and speed to follow tension gradients and persist when canonical sensing is blocked.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Public slime-mould motility movies may cover some gradients but rarely include calibrated surface tension.

obstacles: Public data rarely pair all stimuli with interfacial-tension measurements.
Chemotaxis and osmotaxis provide plausible active rivals.
Aethalium-specific data are sparse.
assessments.rationale: The mechanism can be tested by separating tension gradients from biochemical sensing. Existing public movies offer behavioral proxies but lack the calibrated, orthogonal perturbations needed to resolve the causal account.

assessments.operationalization: Track individual amoeboid cells through active, resting, and encysting phases; quantify sphericity, motility, biochemical activity, and cortical-tension uniformity. Support requires consistent rounding and reduced activity before or during encystment, with active phases showing asymmetric tension and form.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Time-lapse protist datasets can link shape and motility state.

candidate_datasets.name: Cell Image Library
candidate_datasets.role: Public amoeba and protist images provide morphological coverage of active and resting forms.

obstacles: Cell state labels and tension measurements are rarely both present.
Some resting cells remain nonspherical or do not encyst.
Sphericity can reflect wall formation rather than equilibrium.
assessments.rationale: The morphological and activity association is directly measurable in time-lapse data. Public records can test it in selected protists, but the tension mechanism and broad generality remain only partly resolvable.

assessments.operationalization: Measure local membrane or wall tension before and during yeast bud emergence and perturb tension locally while imaging polarity markers. Support requires a local tension drop preceding and inducing expansion, followed by tension-dependent rounding; polarity-driven growth without the predicted drop refutes it.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Live-cell yeast imaging can establish the temporal order of polarity and bud emergence.

obstacles: Direct local tension reporters are uncommon in archived yeast data.
Cell-wall remodeling and polarized actin are strong alternative mechanisms.
assessments.rationale: The proposed temporal sequence and localized mechanical cause are experimentally discriminating. Existing imaging can test morphology and molecular order, but direct tension measurements needed for confirmation are limited.

assessments.operationalization: Reconstruct successive chamber surfaces in living or growth-staged foraminifera and test each new chamber against constant-mean-curvature or minimum-area surfaces under its boundary conditions, while testing the aggregate shell separately. Support requires good fits for new chambers but not for the whole shell and evidence of subsequent rigidification.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Open 3D micro-CT models of foraminiferal tests can support chamber-by-chamber geometric fitting.

candidate_datasets.name: PANGAEA
candidate_datasets.role: Public earth-science datasets include foraminiferal measurements and imagery across taxa and environments.

obstacles: Rigid shells record final rather than fluid chamber geometry.
Boundary conditions and growth-stage timing are often unknown.
Desmid coverage is limited.
assessments.rationale: The geometric prediction is quantifiable from 3D surfaces, and public specimens can test the chamber-versus-whole contrast. The causal role of surface tension during the unobserved fluid stage is harder to establish from finished shells.

assessments.operationalization: Across orders of magnitude in size, calculate surface-to-volume scaling and fit shape responses to interfacial-tension versus gravity, elasticity, and active-stress models. Support requires tension-dominated predictions at cellular or minute scales and systematic loss of predictive power for large-organism form.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Open 3D morphology across organisms provides size and form measurements over broad scales.

obstacles: The transition size depends on material properties and environment.
Shape datasets rarely include all relevant forces.
Taxonomic and scale effects are confounded.
assessments.rationale: The scaling premise yields quantitative dimensionless comparisons and broad counterexample tests. Public morphology is abundant, but matched physical parameters are incomplete, so dominance can be established only for selected systems.

assessments.operationalization: Segment representative unicellular organisms and aggregate cells in 3D, fit all six constant-mean-curvature surface families, and estimate their frequencies and transitions in time-lapse sequences. The claim is supported if sphere, cylinder, and unduloid fits dominate and transitions among them are common.

candidate_datasets.name: Cell Image Library
candidate_datasets.role: Public images across diverse cell types provide a starting sample of unicellular forms.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: 3D and time-lapse microscopy can support surface fitting and transition analysis.

obstacles: Repository sampling is not representative of unicellular diversity.
Many images are 2D projections.
A threshold for classifying approximate surface families is needed.
assessments.rationale: The six candidate geometries permit explicit model selection. Existing images can test selected taxa and dynamics, but biased coverage prevents a reliable estimate of what is commonest across the stated scope.

assessments.operationalization: Measure cylinder radius, cap curvature radius, subtended angle, and cap height from calibrated 3D or optical images of free-ended Spirogyra cells. The law is supported if ratios cluster near 2 for sphere-to-cylinder radius and 0.27 for cap-height-to-cylinder-radius, with deviations linked to unequal tension.

candidate_datasets.name: Cell Image Library
candidate_datasets.role: Public calibrated algal cell images may provide end-cap geometry.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Microscopy datasets can supply higher-resolution or 3D filamentous-alga measurements.

obstacles: Open Spirogyra samples with calibration and free end cells are limited.
2D orientation biases cap measurements.
Wall anisotropy may violate the uniform-tension premise.
assessments.rationale: This is an unusually precise and easily falsified geometric prediction. The analysis is simple, but a sufficiently large, calibrated public sample of the target cells is uncertain.

assessments.operationalization: From calibrated orb-web images, measure coating radius, instability wavelength, bead spacing and size hierarchy, then compare them with Rayleigh-Plateau predictions for a viscous coating on a fiber. Support requires onset near the stated circumference criterion and systematic spacing shifts predicted by viscosity and core drag.

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: Public spider-silk studies may include calibrated microscopy and material measurements.

candidate_datasets.name: Zenodo
candidate_datasets.role: Open microscopy and supplementary datasets can add bead-spacing measurements.

obstacles: Public images may omit fluid radius, viscosity, or time of formation.
Spider chemistry and active spinning introduce additional controls.
assessments.rationale: The instability threshold and spacing are quantitative and distinguish the capillary model from arbitrary beading. Existing open microscopy can test the geometry in subsets, but matched rheology and formation movies are sparse.

assessments.operationalization: Image hydroid calycle rims and stems during secretion, quantify notch and annulation wavelengths, and test whether one surface-tension instability model predicts both geometries and their response to tension perturbation. Distinct developmental patterning or formation after solidification would refute the shared mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Public 3D specimens can quantify final hydroid cup and stem geometry, but not formation mechanics.

obstacles: Final museum morphology does not reveal whether tissue was fluid during patterning.
Developmental time series and tension perturbations are scarce.
The common-cause model lacks a specified parameterization.
assessments.rationale: A shared instability model could yield discriminating geometric and perturbational predictions. Existing specimens mainly record endpoints and are inadequate to establish surface tension as the cause during formation.

assessments.operationalization: Measure directional wall extensibility and cell aspect ratio in freely growing walled cells, perturb wall anisotropy, and fit a mechanical growth model. Support requires anisotropy to precede and quantitatively predict ellipsoidal-to-cylindrical elongation, with isotropization producing rounder cells.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Live plant and algal cell-wall imaging can quantify anisotropic growth.

obstacles: Direct wall extensibility is rarely measured with morphology.
Turgor and cytoskeletal orientation covary with wall anisotropy.
Spirogyra-specific perturbation data are limited.
assessments.rationale: The mechanism gives clear directional measurements and intervention predictions. Existing plant and fungal imaging can test the principle in subsets, but direct mechanics and target-taxon coverage remain incomplete.

assessments.operationalization: Quantify shape diversity across bacteria, protozoa, spores, and free cells and compare it with larger organisms after standardizing dimensionality and sampling; relate within-taxon changes to temperature, osmolarity, and material properties. The claim is supported if small-cell morphospace is consistently restricted and predictable from molecular-scale force models.

candidate_datasets.name: Cell Image Library
candidate_datasets.role: Public images across microorganisms and free cells can define empirical morphospace.

obstacles: Sampling effort differs radically between micro- and macro-organisms.
A 'limited range' needs a defined metric and null model.
Molecular-force dominance is not implied by low diversity alone.
assessments.rationale: Morphospace size and environmental plasticity are measurable with abundant images. The causal inference from limited forms to molecular control is confounded, and representative cross-scale sampling is not available.

assessments.operationalization: Train and validate species classifiers using cell-shape features from bacteria imaged across life stages, growth conditions, and preparation methods, and compare performance with physiological or genomic identifiers. The claim is supported if morphology generalizes poorly across conditions while nonmorphological identity remains stable.

candidate_datasets.name: BioStudies
candidate_datasets.role: Public bacterial imaging studies and supplements provide labeled morphology under varied conditions.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Large microscopy datasets can support cross-condition shape classification.

candidate_datasets.name: BacDive
candidate_datasets.role: Public bacterial phenotypic and physiological records provide nonmorphological identity features and morphology metadata.

obstacles: Repository species labels and imaging protocols may be imbalanced.
Modern high-dimensional morphology may outperform the simple visual criteria Thompson meant.
assessments.rationale: Identification accuracy across controlled domain shifts is a direct test, and extensive public labeled bacterial phenotype and image data exist. The historical word 'seldom' needs a threshold, but comparative performance can robustly resolve the central claim.

assessments.operationalization: Build calibrated 3D outlines of Vorticella bells, fit partial unduloids under the measured stalk and ciliary-ring boundaries, and compare fits with alternative constant-mean-curvature and flexible surfaces. Map fitted parameters across species to test for a continuous cylinder-to-sphere gradation.

candidate_datasets.name: Cell Image Library
candidate_datasets.role: Public ciliate images can provide an initial cross-species sample of bell shapes.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Microscopy datasets may supply calibrated or time-resolved Vorticella morphology.

obstacles: Most public images are 2D and not taxonomically balanced.
Live contraction changes bell shape.
Species identification and boundary-ring dimensions may be missing.
assessments.rationale: The surface family and claimed parameter continuum yield clear geometric model comparisons. Available public imagery likely tests some species but is insufficient for the asserted complete graded series.

assessments.operationalization: Image lorica formation in living protozoa while measuring material adsorption and boundary geometry, then test whether the developing pellicle minimizes area under measured constraints and whether blocking adsorption prevents formation. Protection would be assessed separately through survival experiments and cannot be excluded by geometric fit alone.

candidate_datasets.name: Cell Image Library
candidate_datasets.role: Public protozoan images can test final lorica geometry but usually not formation dynamics.

obstacles: Formation movies and adsorption measurements for the named taxa are scarce.
Minimum-area fit does not distinguish efficient cause from adaptive function.
Lorica materials and boundary conditions vary among taxa.
assessments.rationale: The geometric and adsorption mechanism has measurable consequences, but endpoint images cannot establish inevitability or causal assembly. Existing data are especially weak for separating physical formation from a protective evolutionary function.

assessments.operationalization: Quantify morphological complexity and similarity in minute organisms, then test whether genetically distant or independently sampled lineages converge on identical simple forms more often than complex forms do.

candidate_datasets.name: PR2: Protist Ribosomal Reference database
candidate_datasets.role: Public protist taxonomy and sequence data for estimating genealogical distance among morphologically classified taxa.

candidate_datasets.name: Neotoma Paleoecology Database
candidate_datasets.role: Fossil occurrence and taxonomic records that can test continuity of simple microfossil forms through time.

obstacles: Morphological descriptions and molecular samples rarely come from the same individuals.
Preservation and taxonomic practice can create apparent form identity.
assessments.rationale: The prediction is measurable, but 'physical force' and 'simple characters' require interpretation. Public phylogenetic and fossil records cover useful subsets, while a clean test of common descent is confounded by taxonomy, preservation, and incomplete linkage of form to genotype.

assessments.operationalization: Measure live Lagena orientation during shell deposition and test whether axisymmetric shells grow while vertical whereas flattened or winged shells grow while horizontal.
obstacles: Public shell images do not record orientation during calcification.
Live observations of shell deposition in these taxa are scarce.
assessments.rationale: Orientation, growth state, and shell symmetry give a direct prospective test. Existing occurrence and specimen images show final form but not the organism's posture when that form was produced, so the central temporal variable is missing.

assessments.operationalization: From 3D shell and gonangium images, relate wrinkle orientation to local curvature, diameter, and wall-thickness ratio and compare the observed transition with elastic-shell buckling predictions.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Public 3D specimen scans that can supply surface geometry and wrinkle orientation for some relevant organisms.

obstacles: Wall thickness and in-vivo tension are seldom recorded.
Available scans cover only a subset of the stated taxa.
assessments.rationale: The geometric prediction is precise and modern shell-buckling models provide discriminating alternatives. Public morphology can test wrinkle orientation in subsets, but thickness and loading data needed for the proposed mechanism are often absent.

assessments.operationalization: Measure axopod angles to the local membrane, filament spacing, and intervening membrane curvature in microscopy images, then test whether radiality and honeycomb depressions track the predicted symmetric surface pull.

candidate_datasets.name: Cell Image Library
candidate_datasets.role: Public microscopy images of diverse cells that may include heliozoan and radiolarian surface structures.

obstacles: Static images do not measure surface tension or establish causation.
Relevant taxa are sparsely represented in public image archives.
assessments.rationale: The angular and curvature consequences are measurable, but mapping Thompson's surface-tension attraction to modern cell mechanics is not unique. Existing imagery can assess morphology, while distinguishing tension from cytoskeletal anchoring generally requires perturbation data.

assessments.operationalization: Use ultrastructure and live imaging to test whether the membrane is a fluid film of constant mean curvature lacking active machinery, versus a structurally integrated, actively driven flagellum-attached membrane.

candidate_datasets.name: EMPIAR
candidate_datasets.role: Open electron-microscopy image data for examining trypanosome flagellum and undulating-membrane ultrastructure.

obstacles: Few datasets combine ultrastructure, curvature, and dynamics.
Constant curvature alone would not uniquely identify a passive liquid film.
assessments.rationale: The passive-film model makes clear structural and dynamical predictions that can be compared with active alternatives. Open microscopy resolves major parts of the claim, but comprehensive curvature and force measurements across all named groups are unavailable.

assessments.operationalization: Reconstruct red-cell surfaces, compute mean curvature, and compare observed biconcave and osmotically swollen shapes with equilibrium surface-tension-only models and membrane-mechanics models.

candidate_datasets.name: EMPIAR
candidate_datasets.role: Open electron and cryo-imaging data containing red-cell membrane morphology and ultrastructure.

candidate_datasets.name: Cell Image Library
candidate_datasets.role: Public red-blood-cell images under normal and altered osmotic conditions.

obstacles: Imaging preparation can distort curvature.
The suggested cholesterin mechanism is less directly testable than rejection of surface tension alone.
assessments.rationale: Surface geometry and osmotic shape changes map directly to standard measurements, and equilibrium models yield a decisive comparison. Existing public images are adequate to reject or support the surface-tension-only component, though they do not necessarily identify the exact alternative force.

assessments.operationalization: Order decapod sperm shapes along measured osmotic concentration series and test whether volume loss at nearly constant surface area reproduces normal forms and collapses by solute molarity.

candidate_datasets.name: Cell Image Library
candidate_datasets.role: Public microscopy database that can provide some comparative sperm-cell morphology.

obstacles: Public images rarely include controlled osmolarity metadata.
Species coverage for decapod sperm is limited.
assessments.rationale: The claim specifies an intervention, quantitative dose equivalence, and geometric mechanism. Public morphology can test whether normal forms resemble shrinkage states, but the decisive concentration-series data are scattered or absent.

assessments.operationalization: Co-register cell shape with internal fibril ultrastructure and test whether fibril position, orientation, and elasticity predict spiral form better than membrane forces alone.

candidate_datasets.name: EMPIAR
candidate_datasets.role: Open volume electron-microscopy data for relating cytoskeletal fibrils to whole-cell form.

candidate_datasets.name: Cell Image Library
candidate_datasets.role: Comparative public cell imagery for infusorian and sperm morphology.

obstacles: Elasticity is not inferable reliably from fixed ultrastructure.
Sparse taxonomic coverage limits the broad generalization.
assessments.rationale: Modern cytoskeletal measurements provide a plausible operationalization of 'elastic fibrillae.' Open ultrastructure can test spatial association for selected cells, but causal restraint and mechanical properties usually require new perturbations.

assessments.operationalization: Measure whether membrane or wall constituents enrich at the surface according to their effects on interfacial tension and whether enrichment predicts increased local viscosity and rigidity.

candidate_datasets.name: PRIDE Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Public proteomics data for comparing surface-associated and bulk cellular constituents.

obstacles: Adsorption, active trafficking, and biosynthetic secretion can produce similar enrichment.
Datasets seldom include interfacial tension and rigidity in the same cells.
assessments.rationale: Surface enrichment and mechanics are measurable, but the historical assertion that secretion is 'nothing more' than adsorption is unusually broad. Existing imaging and proteomics resolve components of the model, with serious causal confounding.

assessments.operationalization: Segment cells, vacuoles, and nascent spicules in 3D developmental images and test whether deposition follows interfaces and whether interface geometry predicts spicule geometry.

candidate_datasets.name: EMPIAR
candidate_datasets.role: Open volume electron microscopy suitable for localizing mineral deposits relative to cellular interfaces.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Public 3D scans for comparative mature spicule geometry.

obstacles: Mature scans do not identify the developmental interface.
Open developmental volumes cover few sponge and radiolarian taxa.
assessments.rationale: The localization and geometric-covariation predictions are explicit. Existing 3D data can test selected cases, but the characteristic-generalization across spicule-forming organisms needs broader developmental imaging.

assessments.operationalization: Track cell shape, cortical tension, and membrane or cyst-wall deposition through encystment and test whether deposition starts only after positive tension and rounding.
obstacles: Public time series rarely combine tension measurements with wall-formation markers.
The universal 'only when' condition requires broad taxonomic sampling.
assessments.rationale: A longitudinal test has clear variables and falsification by wall formation before rounding. Current open imaging may show individual encystment sequences, but not the required simultaneous tension and deposition data across the stated scope.

assessments.operationalization: Relate temperature histories to encystment or resting-egg shell thickness while controlling photoperiod, nutrition, and season, and test whether colder conditions consistently increase membrane formation.
obstacles: Season covaries with photoperiod, food, and desiccation.
Occurrence records rarely measure adsorption or capsule strength directly.
assessments.rationale: Temperature and encystment phenology are measurable, but the adsorption mechanism is harder to distinguish from other seasonal cues. Existing records support broad correlational tests rather than a decisive mechanistic resolution.

assessments.operationalization: Test whether mitochondrial and fibrillar structures have stable molecular identities and functions and whether their axial distributions are better predicted by active transport and organelle biogenesis than by passive surface-tension clumping.

candidate_datasets.name: Human Protein Atlas
candidate_datasets.role: Open subcellular localization images and molecular annotations for organelles and fibrillar structures.

obstacles: The claim combines several distinct structures and cell types.
Surface tension and osmotic currents are not directly measured in most archives.
assessments.rationale: Modern molecular and imaging databases can strongly discriminate special organelles from nonspecific clumps for many cell types. The full generalization and proposed physical transport mechanism remain only partly testable from existing archived data.

assessments.operationalization: Map intracellular potassium concentration and local cortical tension in the same cells and test for inverse spatial association and predictable redistribution after tension perturbation.
obstacles: Public datasets rarely co-measure ion concentration and local tension.
Historical cobalt-nitrite staining may not specifically report free potassium.
assessments.rationale: The claimed inverse spatial relation is testable, although 'weak tension' needs a modern mechanical definition. Available public imaging generally supplies either ion localization or mechanics, not both at sufficient resolution.

assessments.operationalization: In time-lapse images, determine whether potassium enrichment and reduced cortical tension precede conjugation bulges or root-hair emergence and disappear when symmetry returns.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Public biological imaging archive that may contain relevant algal or plant-cell morphogenesis series.

obstacles: Relevant time series usually lack potassium sensors and tension measurements.
The claim spans unrelated algal and plant systems.
assessments.rationale: Temporal precedence and colocalization provide clear criteria. Public morphogenesis movies may resolve shape change, but the paired chemical and mechanical channels needed for the mechanism are not generally available.

assessments.operationalization: Quantify potassium at basal bodies and compare it with nearby cortex, then test whether enrichment predicts flagellar protuberances or ciliary ridges independently of basal-body proteins.

candidate_datasets.name: Cell Image Library
candidate_datasets.role: Public ciliate and flagellate images for the morphological portion of the prediction.

Static colocalization would not establish that potassium causes weakened tension.
assessments.rationale: The spatial enrichment claim is directly measurable and potentially discriminating. Existing public images describe basal morphology but generally lack validated potassium maps, leaving the central empirical variable unavailable.

assessments.operationalization: Relate measured local cortical tension or its perturbation to quantified asymmetry across unicellular organisms and compare predictive performance with cytoskeletal and polarity models.

candidate_datasets.name: Cell Image Library
candidate_datasets.role: Broad comparative imagery of unicellular forms.

obstacles: 'Molecular forces' is broad enough to encompass many rival mechanisms.
Tension is usually inferred rather than measured.
assessments.rationale: Shape asymmetry is measurable, but the causal statement is underspecified and risks becoming compatible with nearly any cellular mechanism. Existing imaging can test narrow modern interpretations, not the full generalization.

assessments.operationalization: Reconstruct cell aggregates, estimate interface areas and tensions, and compare observed tissue geometry with constrained minimal-area predictions and models dominated by adhesion, elasticity, or growth.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Public developmental and tissue-imaging datasets across plants and animals.

The claim's tissue-wide scope exceeds available consistently segmented data.
assessments.rationale: Cell interfaces and area minimization are quantitatively testable with standard segmentation and physical models. Data are abundant for selected tissues, but causal attribution chiefly to surface tension remains confounded and overly broad.

assessments.operationalization: Measure junction angles, relative wall age and stiffness, and division timing in plant tissues, testing whether new walls meet already rigid walls perpendicularly more often than equally young walls.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Open plant developmental time-lapse images for wall chronology and junction geometry.

Geometry and division rules offer competing explanations for right angles.
assessments.rationale: The mechanism supplies a clear comparison based on wall age and rigidity. Existing imaging can establish timing and angles for some tissues, but paired mechanical data and broad plant coverage are incomplete.

assessments.operationalization: Infer relative interface tensions from contact angles in paired cells and test whether measured outer shape and partition curvature satisfy the force-balance equations.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Public microscopy for cell-pair and filament geometry.

obstacles: Nostoc and related taxa have limited suitable open 3D data.
Cell walls and active growth can violate fluid-interface assumptions.
assessments.rationale: The force-balance relation makes quantitative, falsifiable geometric predictions. Public images permit tests in selected aggregates, although direct tension measurements and adequate taxonomic coverage are limited.

assessments.operationalization: Segment planar tissue sections, measure junction valence, angles, cell areas, and wall curvature, and test whether triple junctions remain at 120 degrees independent of cell size.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Broad public microscopy collection for cross-tissue replication.

obstacles: Projection and section orientation can bias measured angles.
Rigid or actively stressed tissues may not satisfy equilibrium assumptions.
assessments.rationale: Every element of the law maps directly to standard image-derived variables. Large open image collections and routine segmentation make a decisive test feasible, including quantification of exceptions.

assessments.operationalization: Reconstruct four-cell embryos in 3D and test whether any full-contact configuration has a four-way junction rather than an intervening polar furrow.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Open embryo time-lapse and volumetric microscopy across model animals.

Some species and imaging orientations are underrepresented.
assessments.rationale: The universal topological prediction is exceptionally clear and refuted by a verified four-way full-contact junction. Existing 3D embryo datasets and standard surface reconstruction can test it across several taxa.

assessments.operationalization: Measure contact angles and interface tensions in blastomeres or drop-like cells and test the stated force-balance threshold for transition from finite contact to point contact.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Open embryo imaging for contact-angle and rounding measurements.

Adhesion, cortical elasticity, and pressure complicate the liquid-drop model.
assessments.rationale: The mathematical threshold and morphology are directly operationalizable. Open images can test geometric consequences and selected perturbations, but full tension measurements across blastomeres, pollen, and algae are incomplete.

assessments.operationalization: Compare outer and internal cells with matched lineage and perturb position, testing whether exterior location predicts flattening, rectangularity, and near-right-angle partitions through measured wall mechanics.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Public plant developmental imaging for comparing outer and inner cell geometry.

assessments.rationale: The geometric correlates are measurable, but 'follow as a matter of course' demands causal separation of position from differentiation. Existing comparative images support association tests, not a clean general mechanistic verdict.

assessments.operationalization: Across segmented epithelia, regress hexagon regularity and elongation on cell-size variance and anisotropic stress or growth, testing whether near-perfect regularity is confined to uniform conditions.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Public plant and animal tissue microscopy for comparative tests.

obstacles: Uniform forces are often inferred from shape rather than measured.
Tissue curvature and imaging projection affect apparent regularity.
assessments.rationale: Cell size, sidedness, elongation, and stress anisotropy are standard quantitative variables. Broad open tissue imagery permits a direct comparative test, though interpreting force uniformity requires care.

assessments.operationalization: For packed objects of known size dispersion and contact completeness, measure neighbour number, sidedness, and junction angles and test convergence toward six neighbours and 120-degree junctions.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: 3D scans of biological packed structures such as corals.

Size variation and boundary effects alter neighbour counts.
assessments.rationale: The packing prediction is mathematically precise and straightforward to extract from images. Existing data test several biological subclasses, but not the universal range of materials and force types stated.

assessments.operationalization: Segment colonial coral scans and compare sidedness and circularity between massive close-contact and fasciculate colonies, testing whether mean sidedness is six despite size variation.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Public 3D coral scans for corallite contact, shape, and sidedness.

obstacles: Fossil deformation can alter sidedness.
Some named historical genera have limited digital coverage.
assessments.rationale: Contact state, circularity, and number of sides are directly measurable in existing specimen scans. Public collections are sufficient for a strong test of the main massive-versus-fasciculate and mean-six predictions.

assessments.operationalization: Reconstruct honeycomb cells, measure prism sidedness and basal facet angles, and compare surface area with alternative closures at matched volume.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Public 3D scans that can support quantitative comb-cell geometry where available.

obstacles: Image collections may lack calibrated internal 3D views.
Real comb deformation can obscure ideal angles.
assessments.rationale: The geometry and constrained surface-area comparison are explicit and testable with routine 3D measurement. Public specimen imagery can resolve the anatomical statement, while the minimal-surface calculation is directly reproducible.

assessments.operationalization: Track wax temperature, rheology, and cell-wall geometry during construction and test whether hexagonal and pyramidal forms emerge during a semi-fluid relaxation phase without corrective bee shaping.
obstacles: Public data rarely capture internal comb geometry, wax state, and insect actions simultaneously.
Bee manipulation and thermal relaxation can occur together.
assessments.rationale: The mechanism has clear temporal and physical predictions. Static open images establish final geometry but cannot distinguish passive surface-tension relaxation from active construction, so targeted dynamic data are needed.

assessments.operationalization: Segment equal-sized plant parenchyma cells in 3D, classify face topology and geometry, and compare frequencies of rhombic dodecahedra and fourteen-faced Kelvin-like cells.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Open 3D plant-tissue microscopy for cellular polyhedron reconstruction.

obstacles: Few datasets resolve complete cell faces over large parenchyma volumes.
Cells are rarely equal-sized or perfectly symmetric.
assessments.rationale: The two geometric alternatives are sharply distinguishable in segmented volumes. Existing public microscopy can test selected tissues, but full 3D face resolution and the claim's 'generally' scope are limited.

assessments.operationalization: A test would require a specified set of physical laws that predicts complete later embryo geometry before comparison with 4D developmental images.
obstacles: No particular laws, parameters, or error criterion are stated.
Any material configuration is in some sense governed by physical laws.
assessments.rationale: Abundant embryo datasets exist, but the claim does not state a model whose predictions could fail. Without specifying the 'simple physical laws,' observed configurations cannot discriminate this assertion from its rivals.

assessments.operationalization: Across four-cell embryos, model polar-furrow topology from relative blastomere volumes and test whether size predicts arrangement better than species identity.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Open volumetric embryo time series for cell size and contact topology.

obstacles: Cross-phyla image protocols and stage definitions differ.
Lineage-specific adhesion and cleavage programs covary with species.
assessments.rationale: Cell volumes, furrow arrangement, and taxonomic identity support a direct comparative model. Current open data cover several model species but not the wide phylogenetic scope asserted, and species-level confounding remains.

assessments.operationalization: No dataset can distinguish universal physical governance from replacement by an undefined agency unknown to physics without an independent measurable prediction for that agency.
obstacles: The rival 'unknown vital agency' has no measurable definition.
The assertion is framed as absence of evidence over all development.
assessments.rationale: This is a conceptual rejection of vitalism rather than a bounded empirical model. Because the alternative is undefined and physical forces necessarily act on material tissue, no outcome in an existing dataset uniquely resolves it.

assessments.operationalization: Measure pre-division cell axes and successive wall orientations, comparing observed partitions with the equal-volume least-area plane and the predicted 90-degree alternation.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Open plant-cell time-lapse microscopy for pre-division geometry and wall orientation.

obstacles: Real cells depart from rectangular geometry.
Growth between divisions changes the longest axis.
assessments.rationale: The claim supplies exact geometric optima and angular predictions. Existing time-lapse plant datasets and standard segmentation make both the single-division and successive-division tests feasible.

assessments.operationalization: Reconstruct each cell immediately before division, compute the least-area equal-volume partition under its boundary constraints, and compare it with the observed new wall.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Open 3D and time-lapse plant and embryo division datasets.

obstacles: The phrase 'given space-content can be enclosed' is ambiguous for unequal divisions.
Mechanical and developmental constraints may change the admissible minimum.
assessments.rationale: Modern computational geometry enables a direct observed-versus-optimal comparison in many archived divisions. The broad claim across plant cells and blastomeres and ambiguity about volume ratio prevent complete resolution from currently harmonized data.

assessments.operationalization: For rectangular cells with known daughter-volume ratios, classify new walls as planar, quarter-cylindrical, or spherical-octant-like and test transitions near 0.30 and 0.15.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Open plant developmental microscopy for unequal-division geometry.

obstacles: Suitable 3D unequal divisions are a small subset of archived images.
Cell corners and boundary constraints are not ideal cubes.
assessments.rationale: The numerical thresholds and wall geometries are highly falsifiable. Public plant imaging can test examples, but adequate sample sizes near both thresholds and across the named tissues are uncertain.

assessments.operationalization: Identify quadrant-shaped pre-division cells and measure daughter areas, wall curvature, endpoint angles, arc angle, and radial start position against the stated shortest-bisector solution.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Public algal, plant, and embryo microscopy for division-wall geometry.

obstacles: Quadrant-shaped cells matching the assumptions are uncommon.
Flattening pressure and 3D thickness are often undocumented.
assessments.rationale: This is an unusually precise geometric law with clear confirming values. Existing imagery likely provides restricted examples, but not a broad, purpose-built sample spanning algae and pressure-flattened eggs.

assessments.operationalization: Measure sector angle before division and classify the new wall as anticlinal or periclinal, testing for a transition between 62.5 and 90 degrees and comparing actual wall areas.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Open plant and embryo time-lapse microscopy for sector geometry and division orientation.

obstacles: Few archives annotate pre-division sector angle.
Tissue stress and polarity can override area minimization.
assessments.rationale: The angular interval and binary wall orientation form a direct test. Open imaging permits retrospective analysis in selected tissues, but coverage around the threshold and across the full scope is limited.

assessments.operationalization: Track radial growth, daughter-cell area, and division timing after the asymmetric quadrant split and test the predicted ordering and radius ratios 1.345 versus 1.517.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Potential source of open algal-disc time series for growth and division timing.

obstacles: Relevant long-term Erythrotrichia-like growth series are rare.
Uniform organismal radial growth must be verified independently.
assessments.rationale: The ordering and numerical growth thresholds are sharply testable. Public time-lapse data may resolve individual examples, but datasets matching the idealized initial geometry and uniform growth assumption are sparse.

assessments.operationalization: From lineage-resolved disc growth, test whether successive near-minimal divisions preferentially leave quadrilateral peripheral cells that divide radially and form a parallel-sided outer layer.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Open developmental time series for lineage, topology, and division-wall analysis.

obstacles: Lineage-resolved data for the named algae and cryptogams are limited.
Epidermal identity may also be specified molecularly.
assessments.rationale: The proposed topological sequence is measurable in time-lapse images. Existing developmental data can test restricted plant systems, but they do not broadly isolate minimal-area division as the cause of epidermis formation.

assessments.operationalization: Classify eight-cell partition topology in multiple embryos from the same species and test whether more than one essentially different arrangement occurs.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Open multi-embryo developmental imaging for within-species topology variation.

obstacles: Some datasets contain few embryos per species.
Equivalent 3D arrangements can look different in 2D projections.
assessments.rationale: A single well-imaged species with multiple distinct arrangements refutes constancy, making the criterion simple and decisive. Open embryo datasets with replicates support this analysis now.

assessments.operationalization: Enumerate admissible planar contact graphs for eight surface-reaching cells under triple-junction constraints, then classify observed eight-cell aggregates and test whether all fit exactly thirteen types.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Open eight-cell embryo and plant imaging for observed contact-graph classification.

obstacles: The mathematical count depends sensitively on unstated equivalence and admissibility conventions.
Observed 3D contacts can be ambiguous near vertices.
assessments.rationale: The combinatorial component can be checked exactly and observations can test the empirical universality. Existing images cover important cases, but not every plant and animal drawing or all interpretations of the thirteen-type classification.

assessments.operationalization: For observed small-cell contact graphs, calculate inequality of contact counts and test whether low-inequality topologies persist longer or occur more frequently than concentrated-contact topologies.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Open embryo time series for topology frequency and persistence.

obstacles: Frequency is not identical to mechanical stability.
Lineage programs and sampling can determine topology prevalence.
assessments.rationale: Contact inequality and persistence are measurable, but stability has several possible operational definitions. Existing time series can test association in model systems, while causal attribution and the broad class of oil-drop models remain incomplete.

assessments.operationalization: Classify contact topologies of matched-size cell groups across taxa and test whether a small recurrent set explains most observations and whether topology is independent of classification after geometry is controlled.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Cross-taxon public developmental imaging for cell-contact topology.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Comparative 3D morphology for partitioned organs.

obstacles: 'Small number' and 'same few' lack fixed thresholds.
Public imaging is concentrated in model organisms and homologous stages.
assessments.rationale: The recurrence and taxonomic-independence components admit comparative tests after defining topology classes. Current datasets are taxonomically biased, and the loose quantitative wording weakens discrimination.

assessments.operationalization: Reconstruct coral septal contact topology and test whether fossulae arise among predicted space-partition arrangements without covarying with independent measures of bilateral developmental organization.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Public 3D coral scans for septal and fossular geometry.

obstacles: Higher 'grade of organisation' has no clear modern metric.
Fossil specimens preserve geometry but little developmental evidence.
assessments.rationale: The space-partition account of fossular geometry is testable from scans. The stronger conclusion that a fossula gives no evidence of bilaterality is an inference whose rival is underspecified and poorly served by fossil morphology alone.

assessments.operationalization: Across leaf epidermal images, quantify cell elongation and stomatal row order, testing whether oblong-cell tissues show stronger row alignment than polygonal-cell tissues and whether minimal partitions mediate the relation.

candidate_datasets.name: TRY Plant Trait Database
candidate_datasets.role: Plant trait database useful for species sampling and linking leaf traits to comparative records.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Public plant microscopy for epidermal-cell and stomatal spatial analysis.

obstacles: Open images are not evenly sampled across monocots and dicots.
Venation and developmental patterning can independently impose rows.
assessments.rationale: Cell shape and stomatal spatial order are standard image-derived variables, permitting a strong comparative test. Existing data can test the association in subsets, but the proposed minimal-partition mechanism and broad taxonomic contrast remain confounded.

assessments.operationalization: Relate mature pollen or spore sphericity and retained tetrad facets to evidence for wall maturation timing relative to separation across taxa and developmental image series.

candidate_datasets.name: PalDat
candidate_datasets.role: Public pollen morphology database for scoring mature shape, facets, and tetrad-derived features.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Open developmental microscopy for wall formation and tetrad separation timing.

obstacles: Mature shape alone cannot establish wall-hardening time.
Developmental series and mature morphology are rarely linked for the same taxa.
assessments.rationale: The predicted shape contrast is readily measurable and pollen databases provide broad comparative material. Existing data only partly connect final geometry to the crucial temporal ordering of wall solidification and liberation.

assessments.operationalization: Map cell sidedness, wall orientation, and subsequent bud initiation in cryptogam time series and test whether outgrowths originate disproportionately over triangular cells.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Open plant developmental imaging for linking cell topology to later outgrowth.

obstacles: Cryptogams are sparsely represented in public lineage-resolved imaging.
Cell topology may correlate with pre-existing developmental polarity.
assessments.rationale: The enrichment of buds over triangular cells is a direct statistical prediction. Some archived developmental imaging can test particular systems, but broad cryptogam coverage and causal separation from polarity are weak.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate each apical cell's growth rate, interdivision interval, pre-division shape, and wall orientation, then test whether the growth-to-division ratio predicts the stated transverse, oblique, and axial regimes.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Open plant and algal growth time series for cell shape and division-plane analysis.

obstacles: Suitable apical-cell series for mosses, liverworts, ferns, and algae are limited.
Polarity and tissue stress may confound the growth-rate ratio.
assessments.rationale: All variables can be extracted from sufficiently long time-lapse sequences and the orientation regimes are explicit. Existing datasets permit tests in restricted taxa, but not the full cryptogam scope or a clean causal attribution.

assessments.operationalization: Use time-resolved tissue imaging to compare changes in organ-scale anisotropic growth with cell division orientation and topology. Competing causal models should predict whether tissue geometry precedes and explains cell-network organization or vice versa.

candidate_datasets.name: BioStudies
candidate_datasets.role: Public microscopy studies can supply time-resolved cell segmentation and tissue geometry in selected model organisms.

obstacles: Causal direction is difficult to establish from observational imaging.
The claim spans plants and animals but data are concentrated in model systems.
assessments.rationale: The proposed variables are measurable, but 'overall configuration' and its causal priority require interpretation. Existing developmental imaging can test selected tissues, not the broad scope, and feedback between cell behavior and tissue form is a major confound.

assessments.operationalization: Classify mineral nucleation sites in histological and ultrastructural images by whether they lie inside metabolically active cytoplasm or in extracellular or inactive matrix. The generalization is supported if nucleation overwhelmingly occurs in matrix across representative calcifying and silicifying taxa.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Public cellular and ultrastructural image datasets may show mineral location relative to cells and matrix.

obstacles: Metabolic activity is rarely measured in the same images.
Public images are taxonomically and procedurally biased.
assessments.rationale: Mineral location is directly observable, but the active-versus-inactive distinction often needs proxy markers. Public microscopy can address particular tissues, while the cross-kingdom 'as a rule' scope would require extensive harmonization.

assessments.operationalization: Compare survival, developmental stage, skeletal-rod mineralization and arm length between control and calcium-depleted sea-urchin larvae. The claim is supported by viable stage-matched larvae lacking rods and long arms specifically under calcium depletion.

candidate_datasets.name: BioStudies
candidate_datasets.role: Searchable public study repository for experimental supplements and larval images.

obstacles: A dedicated open replication dataset may not exist.
Lime-free water can cause physiological effects beyond skeleton loss.
assessments.rationale: The treatment and outcomes give a clean experimental test with standard analysis. Public experimental records and images may test some species, but existence of sufficiently documented lime-free experiments is uncertain and the extension beyond echinoids is not covered.

assessments.operationalization: Combine measurements of marine circularly polarized sunlight with wavelength-specific asymmetric photolysis data for plausible prebiotic chiral compounds, then model whether the observed sign and magnitude could generate biological homochirality. Refutation would require showing the mechanism is absent or quantitatively insufficient under plausible early-Earth conditions.
obstacles: Early-Earth illumination and substrates are unobserved.
Present-day optical and laboratory data cannot identify a unique historical cause.
Many competing symmetry-breaking mechanisms make outcomes weakly discriminating.
assessments.rationale: The physical submechanism is testable, but the historical-origin claim requires substantial assumptions about unavailable initial conditions. Existing data could constrain plausibility but cannot resolve whether this process started biological homochirality.

assessments.operationalization: Quantify radial crystal orientation, concentric zoning, polymorph and organic-matrix distribution in images of pearls, otoliths and albumin-grown calcospherites. Shared multiscale structural signatures would support structural equivalence, but mechanism requires distinguishing common precipitation physics from other biomineralization routes.

candidate_datasets.name: Zenodo
candidate_datasets.role: Public repository containing microscopy and tomography datasets from biomineralization studies.

obstacles: Comparable raw images across all three materials are scattered.
Structural similarity alone does not establish identical formation mechanism.
assessments.rationale: Modern imaging makes the morphological comparison direct. Data are likely available piecemeal, but the mechanistic inference is underdetermined because similar zoning can arise through distinct matrix-controlled processes.

assessments.operationalization: For dated growth-zone series, test whether increments align reliably with independent seasonal or diel markers and compare externally forced versus endogenous reaction-diffusion models. Finding internally generated periodicity or poor alignment would refute the assumption that visible rings necessarily record external cycles.

candidate_datasets.name: PANGAEA
candidate_datasets.role: Public environmental and sclerochronological time-series data can link growth increments to external conditions.

obstacles: Different structures have different ring-forming mechanisms.
Environmental covariates and internal rhythms can be correlated.
assessments.rationale: The modest claim rejects necessity rather than all environmental control, so a single well-supported endogenous counterexample is informative. Open sclerochronology and environmental series can test several systems, though not the entire heterogeneous scope.

assessments.operationalization: Measure calcium carbonate and phosphate solubility and precipitation kinetics as intact albumins are enzymatically degraded, while controlling pH, carbonate and competing ions. Support requires protein breakdown to precede and quantitatively explain mineral precipitation better than direct acid-base chemistry.
obstacles: Public datasets rarely combine proteolysis kinetics with mineral supersaturation.
In vivo calcification includes active ion transport and specialized matrix proteins.
assessments.rationale: The chemical mechanism has measurable variables and experimentally separable rivals. However, suitable paired kinetic data appear unlikely to exist openly, and extrapolation from simplified solutions to all calcified tissues would remain inadequate.

assessments.operationalization: Across skeletal elements spanning orders of magnitude, estimate geometric scaling of surface, gravitational and loading stresses and compare form with predicted dominant-force regimes. Support requires a reproducible size transition from surface- or molecular-force signatures to load-adapted geometry.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Open 3D models provide skeletal geometry over a broad size and taxonomic range.

obstacles: Force dominance is inferred rather than directly observed.
Material composition, phylogeny and function covary with scale.
assessments.rationale: Scaling predictions are measurable, but 'molecular forces' is broad and requires modern reinterpretation. Morphological data support a comparative test, yet confounding and sparse microscopic taxa limit a clean general conclusion.

assessments.operationalization: Reconstruct the contemporaneous cell surface and spicule centerline in 3D, then test whether the centerline has near-zero geodesic curvature and fits the shortest surface path better than unconstrained growth models. Multiple developmental stages would test the proposed confinement mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: EMPIAR
candidate_datasets.role: Open electron microscopy image archive that may include suitable sponge cellular ultrastructure.

obstacles: Adult spicules do not preserve the cell surface that constrained growth.
Matched developmental 3D images are rare.
assessments.rationale: Geodesicity has an explicit geometric test. Existing archives may contain spicule ultrastructure, but likely lack simultaneous high-resolution cell-surface reconstructions needed to resolve the mechanism.

assessments.operationalization: Extract quantitative shape descriptors for siliceous sponge and calcitic holothurian spicules and test convergence after controlling for developmental compartment geometry. Similar shapes across materials support material-independence only if within-material and cell-confinement alternatives are modeled.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Public specimen scans may provide comparative spicule morphology.

obstacles: Similarity across materials does not by itself identify the shaping force.
Comparable developmental cell geometry is generally absent.
assessments.rationale: The morphological premise is testable with existing specimens and images. The conclusion that chemistry is irrelevant and confinement causal is weakly discriminated by morphology alone, so only part of the claim can be resolved.

assessments.operationalization: Measure ray angles and curvature in 3D spicules and, where developmental imaging exists, compare ray trajectories with three- and four-cell junctions. Support requires clustering near 120 and 109.47 degrees for equal-cell junctions and predictable deviations with unequal cells.

candidate_datasets.name: EMPIAR
candidate_datasets.role: Open volumetric electron microscopy can provide cellular junction and spicule geometry in selected specimens.

obstacles: Matched developing-cell and spicule datasets are scarce.
Crystal growth constraints can generate similar angles.
assessments.rationale: The angular predictions are precise and readily analyzed. Public morphology can test angle distributions, but resolving formation at cell junctions needs rare developmental volumes and controls for crystallography.

assessments.operationalization: Reconstruct vesicle centers and nascent six-rayed spicules in developing hexactinellids, classify packing as cubic or close-packed, and test whether ray axes follow cubic nearest-neighbor directions. A close-packed arrangement with unchanged spicule geometry would refute the mechanism.
obstacles: Developmental 3D data for glass sponges are exceptionally scarce.
Mature skeletons cannot uniquely recover prior vesicle packing.
assessments.rationale: The packing mechanism makes a clear geometric prediction. Existing specimen data can show six-rayed geometry but are unlikely to contain the developmental vesicle arrangement required for a discriminating test.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate species range sizes, occupancy, local richness, dominance and fossil first occurrences from georeferenced living and fossil records, with standardized sampling and taxonomic validation. The claim predicts unusually broad ranges, high local richness, weak dominance and long genus or family durations.

candidate_datasets.name: Ocean Biodiversity Information System
candidate_datasets.role: Public georeferenced occurrence records for living marine Radiolaria.

candidate_datasets.name: Paleobiology Database
candidate_datasets.role: Public fossil occurrences for evaluating temporal ranges and ancient records.

obstacles: Micropaleontological taxonomy has substantial synonymy and revision.
Sampling effort is highly uneven in space, depth and geological time.
assessments.rationale: Distribution and assemblage claims map directly to occurrence records, and large open databases exist. Biases and incomplete identification weaken global and Cambrian-era conclusions, but major parts are presently testable.

assessments.operationalization: Relate particle incorporation probabilities to particle size, shape, chemistry and measured interfacial energies in time-lapse observations of shell building. A surface-energy model must predict selectivity and assembly without organismal transport behavior better than active-choice models.
obstacles: Surface energy is not usually measured alongside particle-selection behavior.
Active cytoskeletal transport and passive trapping can coexist.
assessments.rationale: The mechanism can be formalized, but 'purely physical' requires excluding active biological processes. Existing images of agglutinated tests lack the simultaneous behavioral and interfacial measurements needed for that discrimination.

assessments.operationalization: Co-register developing vesicle boundaries and silica deposition in 3D and quantify whether rods arise specifically in intervesicular grooves, with mesh regularity tracking vesicle size variance and layers tracking repeated vesicle shells. Alternative cytoskeletal templates should be compared.

candidate_datasets.name: EMPIAR
candidate_datasets.role: Potential source of open ultrastructural volumes for protist silicification.

obstacles: Suitable live or staged radiolarian ultrastructure is rare.
Adult lattice geometry does not uniquely reveal the deposition template.
assessments.rationale: The mechanism gives clear spatial and correlational predictions. Public imaging may describe mature shells, but matched developmental vesicle and silica maps across the named taxa are unlikely to be adequate.

assessments.operationalization: Compare lattice regularity and topology across silica-, celestite- and organic-skeleton taxa using standardized images, then test whether material predicts form after phylogeny and size are controlled. Demonstrating an underlying vesicular template requires direct developmental imaging rather than cross-material convergence alone.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Public 3D media for comparing skeletal lattice geometry across specimens.

obstacles: Cross-material convergence is not unique evidence for vesicle moulding.
The groups differ in phylogeny, ecology and scale.
assessments.rationale: Material-independence of gross form is measurable from existing morphology. The stronger causal inference to an underlying vesicular structure remains poorly discriminated without developmental observations.

assessments.operationalization: Reconstruct Callimitra skeletons and developing cells in 3D, testing for six interfaces, triple junctions near 120 degrees and tetrahedral edge angles near 109.47 degrees with direct colocalization at cell boundaries. Development without four-cell contact would refute the asserted necessity.
obstacles: Modern developmental imaging of Callimitra is likely absent.
A tetrahedral skeleton can arise from non-cellular geometric processes.
assessments.rationale: The geometry is precise, but mature shape alone cannot establish where it formed. The necessary developmental cellular context is too specialized to expect adequate public data.

assessments.operationalization: Measure face, edge and angle equality in 3D polyhedral radiolarian specimens to determine whether regular dodecahedra and icosahedra truly occur. If regularity is confirmed, compare the structure with crystallographic periodic tessellation predictions, while distinguishing crystal lattice formation from broader space-partitioning mechanisms.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Open 3D specimen data can test whether purported polyhedra are geometrically regular.

obstacles: Haeckel's drawings may idealize specimen geometry.
Noncrystallographic dodecahedra do not exclude every space-partitioning process.
assessments.rationale: Modern geometry can test the critical descriptive premise and periodic crystals indeed constrain rotational symmetry. Available 3D coverage is uncertain, and the broader mechanistic exclusion is less direct than the morphological test.

assessments.operationalization: Digitize 3D spine directions in twenty-spined specimens and fit the hexagonal 2+6+6+6 arrangement against Müller's five four-spined circles using angular residuals. Taxon-level model support would directly confirm which arrangement applies.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Public 3D models may permit direct measurement of radial-spine arrangements.

obstacles: Suitable intact microscopic 3D specimens may be sparse.
The assertion that Müller's pattern fits no case requires broad taxonomic coverage.
assessments.rationale: The rival arrangements make precise, mutually distinguishable predictions and analysis is straightforward once 3D data exist. Public coverage can likely test examples but not the universal rejection across all relevant taxa.

assessments.operationalization: In developing Radiolaria, temporally map polarity markers, central cytoplasmic organization, peripheral vesicles and nascent spines, then perturb candidate central and peripheral mechanisms. The claim predicts central polarity before spine placement and persistence when peripheral mechanics are altered.
obstacles: The proposed 'directive forces' have no unique modern observable.
Developmental perturbation data for these organisms are lacking.
Absence of an obvious peripheral mechanism is not evidence for a central force.
assessments.rationale: A modernized central-versus-peripheral origin can be tested, but Thompson's positive force concept is underspecified. Existing mature morphology cannot establish temporal or causal origin, making new developmental data necessary.

assessments.operationalization: Fit centerlines of annular, longitudinal and helical wall thickenings to geodesics on reconstructed cylindrical cell, vessel and tracheal surfaces. Support requires low geodesic curvature compared with plausible nongeodesic curves across the named structures.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Open microscopy datasets can supply 3D plant vascular and insect tracheal geometry.

obstacles: Real biological tubes depart from ideal cylinders.
Pattern classes may be visually described without enough resolution for geodesic fitting.
assessments.rationale: The geometric criterion is explicit and standard image analysis is feasible. Existing images can test representative structures, though cross-taxon coverage and deviations from cylindrical geometry limit the full generalization.

assessments.operationalization: Reconstruct high-spired shells, model the local shell envelope as a cone and compare the sutural and parallel striation paths with calculated surface geodesics. The claim is supported if their geodesic residuals are low and coil spacing decreases toward the apex as predicted.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Open 3D gastropod shell models allow cone fitting and geodesic-path analysis.

obstacles: Shell surfaces are only approximately conical.
Erosion or ornament can obscure sutures and striations.
assessments.rationale: This is a precise geometric statement testable from existing 3D shell scans with standard methods. Broad enough Turritella and related material is publicly represented to confirm or refute the principal claim.

assessments.operationalization: On 3D curved biological surfaces, extract crossing line systems and test each family for low geodesic curvature, then estimate how often reticulation is generated by two such families rather than branching or cellular tiling. A representative prevalence estimate would address the phrase 'very common.'

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Public microscopy offers examples of reticulated patterns on biological surfaces.

obstacles: The scope and threshold for 'very common' are unspecified.
Many reticula arise through branching networks or cell packing.
assessments.rationale: Individual cases can be tested geometrically, but the frequency claim requires defining a sampling universe and compiling diverse structures. Open images support restricted tests rather than a decisive general prevalence estimate.

assessments.operationalization: Map muscle-fibre trajectories onto 3D organ surfaces and compute geodesic curvature and path length relative to endpoint-matched shortest paths. Developmental or mechanical data must additionally test whether tension causes alignment rather than merely correlating with it.

candidate_datasets.name: HuBMAP Data Portal
candidate_datasets.role: Open spatial imaging and tissue maps for human hollow organs.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Public 3D microscopy from model organisms can provide fibre orientation.

obstacles: Anatomical fibre tracts often have changing insertion points and layered helices.
Geodesic alignment does not prove automatic tension-driven arrangement.
assessments.rationale: Fibre geometry is measurable in modern 3D datasets, and representative organs can be analyzed quickly. The causal 'automatically' mechanism and broad organ scope remain confounded by development and function.

assessments.operationalization: Register embryonic heart and stomach tube stages to later organ surfaces, track fibre lineages, and test whether trajectories remain geodesic after deformation and whether shorter paths predict contraction efficiency. Compare with active fibre-remodeling models.

candidate_datasets.name: BioImage Archive
candidate_datasets.role: Open developmental imaging may provide fibre and surface geometry.

obstacles: Lineage-resolved fibre tracking across twisting stages is uncommon.
Fibres differentiate and remodel during organogenesis rather than simply deforming passively.
assessments.rationale: Parts of the geometry can be tested in developmental atlases, but 'remain geodetic' requires longitudinal correspondence rarely present. Efficiency and persistence claims have multiple developmental and biomechanical rivals.

assessments.operationalization: Track 3D position and body orientation of swimming microorganisms, estimating axial rotation, body-fixed curvature and helix pitch. The mechanism is supported when observed trajectories follow parameters predicted from rotation and swerve and become circular when rotation approaches zero.

candidate_datasets.name: BioStudies
candidate_datasets.role: Public supplementary microscopy videos can provide organism trajectories and body orientation.

obstacles: Many videos are two-dimensional.
Phototaxis, boundaries and fluid flow can perturb paths.
assessments.rationale: The kinematic mechanism has precise and discriminating predictions, and published open videos cover multiple ciliated and flagellated swimmers. Standard tracking can resolve the core claim, though not every taxon in its broad scope.

assessments.operationalization: Fit logarithmic and alternative spiral models to digitized horns, shell trajectories, foraminiferal coils and sunflower parastichies, using out-of-sample residuals and parameter constancy. The universal claim is refuted by robust nonlogarithmic examples within any included class.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Open 3D scans of horns, shells and foraminifera for curve fitting.

candidate_datasets.name: iNaturalist
candidate_datasets.role: Public images provide broad examples of sunflower heads and external biological spirals.

obstacles: Perspective and sectioning can distort fitted spirals.
Sunflower phyllotaxis is a point pattern rather than a single permanent curve.
assessments.rationale: The claimed universality and named exception are directly falsifiable with abundant public morphology. Standard model comparison can determine whether logarithmic spirals fit better than Archimedean or variable-pitch alternatives.

assessments.operationalization: Model and compare growing structures under fixed laboratory-frame versus body-rotating deflection fields, then test whether shell growth orientation and columellar-muscle geometry predict the observed spiral. A stable spiral under a demonstrably external fixed-direction force would refute necessity.
obstacles: Growth-force direction is rarely measured in existing datasets.
Multiple intrinsic growth asymmetries can mimic muscle deflection.
The mathematical necessity depends on idealized force assumptions.
assessments.rationale: The fixed-versus-body-frame distinction is formalizable, but morphology alone cannot recover force direction. Existing shell scans are inadequate to identify the proposed columellar-muscle mechanism without new developmental or mechanical measurements.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate local longitudinal and transverse accretion rates from successive growth increments and test whether their ratio is constant and predicts a constant-angle logarithmic centerline. Variable ratios should predict systematic departures from logarithmic form.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Open 3D shells and horns preserve successive accretion geometry for growth-ratio estimation.

obstacles: Static growth lines are proxies for rates.
Tube cross-section and torsion can complicate the ideal model.
assessments.rationale: The claim supplies a quantitative relation between measurable ratios and spiral angle. Existing accretionary hard parts retain growth histories, allowing standard geometric tests across representative shells and horns.

assessments.operationalization: Digitize shoot origins, angles and lengths in scorpioid and helicoid cymes and test constancy of angle and length ratio, then fit the shoot tangents to logarithmic versus alternative spirals. Three-dimensional reconstruction can remove the superimposed helicoid twist.
